In `MetricPoller.send()`: Dequeues availability metrics for processing.

This method: 1. Retrieves pending availability metrics from the queue 2. Groups them by IP address to avoid duplicate polling 3. Batches them for efficient processing (up to 200 metrics per worker) 4. Decrements the idle worker count for each batch created

The method handles duplicate IP addresses by: - Keeping only one metric for each unique IP in the batch - Storing duplicates in the duplicateMetrics map for later processing

It also implements a probing mechanism to avoid infinite loops when: - No more metrics are available - No more idle workers are available @return A list of maps, where each map contains IP-to-metric mappings for a batch / private List> dequeue() { var metrics = new ArrayList>(); var probes = 0; var batchSize = 200; //1 worker means 200 availability metrics... try { while (idleAvailabilityWorkers > 0 && probes < 5) // if probe is greater than 5 means metrics not present or worker not available { for (var pendingMetrics : pendingAvailabilityMetrics.values()) { if (idleAvailabilityWorkers > 0) { var iterator = pendingMetrics.iterator(); if (iterator.hasNext()) { var metric = new HashMap(); metrics.add(metric); var count = 0; while (count < batchSize && iterator.hasNext()) { var id = iterator.next(); if (MetricCacheStore.getStore().queuedMetric(id)) { var event = MetricCacheStore.getStore().dequeue(id); if (EventCacheStore.getStore().validItem(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID))) { count++; EventBusConstants.updateEvent(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID), String.format(InfoMessageConstants.EVENT_TRACKER_EVENT_QUALIFIED, DateTimeUtil.timestamp())); // if two same ip polls collides because of any reason than we will ping for any one & equivalent result will be sent if (metric.containsKey(event.getString(OBJECT_IP))) { duplicateMetrics.computeIfAbsent(event.getString(OBJECT_IP), value -> new ArrayList<>()); duplicateMetrics.get(event.getString(OBJECT_IP)).add(event); } else { metric.put(event.getString(OBJECT_IP), event); } } } else { abort(id); } iterator.remove(); } idleAvailabilityWorkers--; } else { probes++; } } else { probes++; } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } return metrics; } / Sends error information for multiple contexts.

This method iterates through a map of contexts and processes each one with the extract method, which formats the error information and sends it. After processing each context, it removes it from the map to free up memory and prevent duplicate processing.

The method determines the appropriate error message based on the error code: - For PROCESS_TIMEOUT errors: Uses the PROCESS_TIMED_OUT message - For other errors: Uses the INTERNAL_ERROR message @param contexts A map of target IPs to JsonObject contexts to process @param errorCode The error code to set for all contexts @param error The detailed error information (stack trace), can be null

In `ObjectConfigStore.updateItemsByUser()`: Updates the itemsByProfile and itemsByUser maps for a specific object ID based on group membership. This method evaluates whether the given object qualifies for access by various user profiles and users based on the groups the object belongs to.

The method performs two main operations:

  • Profile-based access: For GROUP-scoped profiles, checks if the object belongs to any of the profile's groups and updates the itemsByProfile map accordingly
  • User-based access: For users, checks if the object belongs to any of the user's groups and updates the itemsByUser map accordingly. The default user (ID = 1) has access to all objects

Access qualification logic:

  • For profiles: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the profile's groups (ENTITIES)
  • For users: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the user's groups (USER_GROUPS)
  • Default user: Always has access to all objects regardless of group membership

This method should be called when:

  • An object's groups are modified (added/removed)
  • A new object is added to the system with group assignments
  • Object group membership changes that affect user/profile access

    protected void cloneTemplate(RoutingContext routingContext) {

        JsonObject jsonObject = routingContext.body().asJsonObject();

        Long templateId = jsonObject.getLong(ID);

        String templateName = jsonObject.getString(ENTITY_PROPERTY_NAME);

        try {
            LOGGER.info("Starting template cloning process for template ID: " + templateId);

            var template = TemplateConfigStore.getStore().getItem(templateId);

            if (template == null || template.isEmpty()) {

                LOGGER.warn("Template not found for cloning: " + templateId);

                this.send(routingContext, new JsonObject()
                        .put(RESPONSE_CODE, HttpStatus.SC_BAD_REQUEST)
                        .put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL)
                        .put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_BAD_REQUEST)
                        .put(MESSAGE, "Template not found with ID: " + templateId)
                );
                return;
            }

            template.remove(ID);

            template.put(TEMPLATE_NAME, templateName);

            LOGGER.info("Prepared cloned template structure with name: Copy of " + templateName);

            cloneTemplateWidgets(template)
                    .compose(v -> saveClonedTemplate(template))
                    .compose(parentTemplateId -> {
                        // Clone child templates
                        var childTemplates = TemplateConfigStore.getStore().getItemsByValue(TEMPLATE_PARENT_ID, templateId);

                        var cloneWidgetFutures = new ArrayList<Future<Void>>();

                        for (int i = 0; i < childTemplates.size(); i++) {

                            var childTemplate = childTemplates.getJsonObject(i);

                            childTemplate.put(TEMPLATE_PARENT_ID, parentTemplateId);

                            cloneWidgetFutures.add(cloneTemplateWidgets(childTemplate));
                        }

                        return Future.all(cloneWidgetFutures)
                                .compose(widgetCloneResult -> {

                                    var saveTemplateFutures = new ArrayList<Future<Long>>();

                                    for (int i = 0; i < childTemplates.size(); i++) {

                                        var childTemplate = childTemplates.getJsonObject(i);

                                        childTemplate.remove(ID);

                                        childTemplate.put(TEMPLATE_NAME, "Copy of " + childTemplate.getString(TEMPLATE_NAME));

                                        saveTemplateFutures.add(saveClonedTemplate(childTemplate));
                                    }

                                    return Future.all(saveTemplateFutures).compose(e-> Future.succeededFuture(parentTemplateId));

                                });
                    })
                    .onSuccess(parentTemplateId -> {

                        LOGGER.info("Template cloned successfully");

                        this.send(routingContext, new JsonObject()
                                .put(RESPONSE_CODE, HttpStatus.SC_OK)
                                .put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_SUCCEED)
                                .put(MESSAGE, "Template cloned successfully")
                                .put(RESULT, parentTemplateId)
                        );
                    })
                    .onFailure(error -> {

                        LOGGER.error(error);

                        this.send(routingContext, new JsonObject()
                                .put(RESPONSE_CODE, HttpStatus.SC_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
                                .put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL)
                                .put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR)
                                .put(MESSAGE, "Failed to clone template: " + error)
                        );
                    });

        } catch (Exception exception) {
            LOGGER.error(exception);

            this.send(routingContext, new JsonObject()
                    .put(RESPONSE_CODE, HttpStatus.SC_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)
                    .put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL)
                    .put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR)
                    .put(MESSAGE, "Failed to clone template: " + exception.getMessage())
            );
        }
    }

    private void assign(RoutingContext routingContext)

            if (schema != null)

                var id = CommonUtil.getLong(routingContext.request().getParam(ID));

                var item = this.configStore.getItem(id);

                if (item != null)
                {
                    Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CHANGE_LOCAL_NOTIFICATION,

                else

                    this.send(routingContext, new JsonObject().put(RESPONSE_CODE, SC_BAD_REQUEST)
                            .put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, STATUS_FAIL)

    /**
     * Helper method to clone template widgets with proper async handling.
     *
     * @param template The template being cloned
     *
     */
    private Future<Void> cloneTemplateWidgets(JsonObject template)
    {
        Promise<Void> promise = Promise.promise();
        try
        {

            if (!template.containsKey("template.widgets"))
            {
                promise.complete(null);

                return Future.succeededFuture();
            }

            var templateWidgets = template.getJsonArray("template.widgets");

            if (templateWidgets.isEmpty())
            {
                LOGGER.debug("Empty widgets array for template");

                promise.complete();

                return Future.succeededFuture();
            }

            var futures = new ArrayList<Future<Void>>();

            LOGGER.info("Starting to clone " + templateWidgets.size() + " widgets");


            for (var i = 0; i < templateWidgets.size(); i++)
            {
                var item = templateWidgets.getJsonObject(i);

                if (item.containsKey(ID))
                {
                    // Retrieve the full widget from WidgetConfigStore
                    var widgetContext = WidgetConfigStore.getStore().getItem(item.getLong(ID));

                    widgetContext.put(VisualizationConstants.VISUALIZATION_NAME, String.format("Copy of %s", widgetContext.getString(VisualizationConstants.VISUALIZATION_NAME)));

                    widgetContext.remove(ID);

                    widgetContext.put("_type","1");

                    Promise<Void> widgetPromise = Promise.promise();

                    Bootstrap.configDBService().save(DBConstants.TBL_WIDGET, widgetContext, DEFAULT_USER, SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS, asyncResult ->
                    {
                        if (asyncResult.succeeded())
                        {
                            WidgetConfigStore.getStore().addItem(asyncResult.result()).onComplete(handler ->
                            {
                                if (handler.succeeded())
                                {
                                    item.put(ID, asyncResult.result());

                                    widgetPromise.complete();
                                }
                                else
                                {
                                    LOGGER.trace(handler.cause().getMessage());

                                    widgetPromise.fail(handler.cause());
                                }
                            });
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            LOGGER.info(asyncResult.cause().getMessage());

                            widgetPromise.fail(asyncResult.cause());
                        }
                    });
                    futures.add(widgetPromise.future());
                }
            }


            Future.all(futures).onComplete(result ->
            {
                if (result.succeeded())
                {
                    LOGGER.info("All widget clones completed successfully, saving template");

                    promise.complete(null);

                }
                else
                {
                    LOGGER.warn("Some widget clones failed: " + result.cause().getMessage());

                    promise.fail("Failed to clone some widgets: " + result.cause().getMessage());
                }
            });

            return promise.future();
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);

            promise.fail(String.format(INTERNAL_SERVER_EXCEPTION, exception.getMessage()));

            return promise.future();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Helper method to save the cloned template to the database.
     *
     * @param template The template to save
     *
     */
    private Future<Long> saveClonedTemplate(JsonObject template)
    {

        template.put("_type","1");

        Promise<Long> promise = Promise.<Long>promise();

        Bootstrap.configDBService().save(DBConstants.TBL_TEMPLATE, template,
                GlobalConstants.DEFAULT_USER, GlobalConstants.SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS,
                result ->
                {
                    if (result.succeeded())
                    {
                        var newTemplateId = result.result();

                        LOGGER.info("Successfully saved cloned template with ID: " + newTemplateId);

                        // Add to TemplateConfigStore
                        TemplateConfigStore.getStore().addItem(newTemplateId).onComplete(asyncResult ->
                        {
                            if (asyncResult.succeeded())
                            {
                                promise.complete(newTemplateId);
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                LOGGER.warn("Failed to add cloned template to store: " + asyncResult.cause().getMessage());

                                promise.fail(asyncResult.cause());
                            }
                        });
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        LOGGER.warn("Failed to save cloned template to database: " + result.cause().getMessage());

                        promise.fail(result.cause());
                    }
                });

        return promise.future();
    }

This class handles different types of events including:

  • Backup and restore operations
  • Application lifecycle events (start, stop, restart)
  • Upgrade events
  • State change notifications
  • Manager upgrade events

This class extends Vert.x's AbstractVerticle to leverage the event-driven, non-blocking programming model for handling concurrent operations efficiently.

ZeroMQ (ZMQ) server implementation for the Motadata transport layer.

This class provides a ZeroMQ-based transport server that supports multiple socket modes for different messaging patterns. It implements the {@link TransportServer} interface to provide a standardized transport abstraction layer for server-side operations.

The server supports different ZeroMQ socket patterns:

  • PUB (Sender): Publishes messages to multiple SUB receivers
  • PULL: Receives messages from multiple PUSH clients in a round-robin fashion
  • PUSH: Sends messages to PULL sockets in a load-balanced manner

Key features:

  • Configurable High Water Mark (HWM) for message queuing and flow control
  • TCP keep-alive support for connection reliability
  • Automatic handling of slow receivers (XPUB_NODROP)
  • Thread-safe message handling with atomic operations
  • Integration with Vert.x event bus for message routing
  • Support for both binding and connecting modes

Configuration example:

{@code   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put("SOCKET_MODE", "PUB")       .put("HOST", "localhost")       .put("PORT", 5555)       .put("EVENT_TYPE", "remote.events");     ZMQServer server = new ZMQServer(config);   server.bind().onSuccess(v -> {       // Server is ready to accept connections       server.send("topic", "Hello World".getBytes());   });   }

Thread Safety: This class is thread-safe for concurrent access to its public methods. However, the underlying ZMQ socket operations are performed in dedicated threads.

In `MotadataAppManager.initializeManager()`: The MotadataAppManager class is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the Motadata application.

This class serves as the central control system for the Motadata application, handling operations such as:

  • Starting, stopping, and restarting application components
  • Managing application upgrades and patches
  • Handling backup and restore operations
  • Coordinating communication between distributed components
  • Managing HTTP servers and event bus handlers
  • Monitoring system health and status

The MotadataAppManager extends Vert.x's AbstractVerticle to leverage the event-driven, non-blocking programming model for handling concurrent operations efficiently. It interacts with various system components through the event bus and maintains the overall state of the application.

This class implements a robust error handling mechanism and ensures proper coordination between different components during critical operations like upgrades and restarts.

Architecture and Design

The MotadataAppManager follows a reactive, event-driven architecture:

  • Event Processing: The class processes events received through the Vert.x event bus, dispatching them to appropriate handler methods based on event type.
  • Asynchronous Operations: All operations are performed asynchronously using Vert.x's Future/Promise pattern to ensure non-blocking behavior.
  • Component Management: The class manages the lifecycle of child processes and components, ensuring they are started, stopped, and monitored appropriately.
  • HTTP Server: The class sets up and manages an HTTP server for handling web-based operations and API endpoints.

Event Handling

The MotadataAppManager handles various types of events:

  • Lifecycle Events: Start, stop, restart events for application components
  • State Change Events: Enable, disable events for components
  • Upgrade Events: Events for upgrading application components or the manager itself
  • Backup/Restore Events: Events for backing up and restoring system data
  • Heartbeat Events: Events for monitoring system health
  • Switchover Events: Events for high availability operations

File Operations

The class performs various file operations for backup, restore, and upgrade:

  • Copying and transferring files between directories
  • Extracting and processing ZIP archives
  • Reading and writing configuration files
  • Managing system files and directories

Process Management

The MotadataAppManager manages external processes:

  • Starting and stopping child processes
  • Monitoring process health and status
  • Handling process output and errors
  • Managing process IDs and registration

Error Handling

The class implements comprehensive error handling:

  • All operations return Futures that can be composed and chained
  • Exceptions are caught, logged, and propagated appropriately
  • Error messages are standardized and include error codes
  • Recovery mechanisms are implemented for critical operations

Usage

The MotadataAppManager is typically used by:

  • System bootstrap processes to initialize the application
  • Administrative interfaces to control application lifecycle
  • Monitoring systems to track application health
  • Upgrade and maintenance processes to perform system updates

Processes network flow data by enriching it with additional information and transforming it for analysis.

The FlowProcessor is a core component of the flow processing system that receives raw flow data from the FlowListener and performs the following operations:

  • Enriches flow data with geolocation information (country, city, coordinates)
  • Adds Autonomous System (AS) information to source and destination IPs
  • Decodes IP addresses and resolves them to hostnames when possible
  • Translates protocol numbers to protocol names
  • Decodes Type of Service (ToS) values
  • Interprets TCP flags
  • Maps interface indices to interface names
  • Calculates traffic metrics (bytes per second, packets per second, etc.)
  • Formats the enriched data for storage and analysis

The processor uses various configuration stores to retrieve mapping information and settings that control how flow data is processed and enriched.

After processing, the enriched flow data is published to the event bus for consumption by other components such as the FlowStatCalculator and storage systems.

/**
 * Processes OpenTelemetry (OTLP) metrics data for JVM monitoring and forwards them to storage and visualization systems.
 *
 * <p>This verticle handles various types of JVM metrics including:
 * <ul>
 *   <li>Memory usage metrics (heap/non-heap, pool-specific)</li>
 *   <li>Garbage collection metrics (duration, count)</li>
 *   <li>Class loading metrics (loaded, unloaded, total classes)</li>
 *   <li>Thread metrics (count, state, daemon status)</li>
 * </ul>
 *
 * <p>Configuration is loaded from {@code trace-metric-parser.json} which defines:
 *
 * <p>Metrics are processed in batches per resource and all internal state is cleared between resource
 * processing cycles to prevent cross-contamination.
 */
public class TraceMetricProcessor extends AbstractVerticle
{
    private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(TraceMetricProcessor.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_TRACE, "Trace Metric Processor");
    private final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder();
    private final Map<String, Map<String, Number>> jvmMemoryMetrics = new HashMap<>();
    private final JsonObject jvmScalarMetrics = new JsonObject();
    private final Map<String, Integer> jvmClassMetrics = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Map<String, Float>> jvmGcMetrics = new HashMap<>();
    private EventEngine eventEngine;
    private Set<String> mappers;

    @Override
    public void start(Promise<Void> promise) throws Exception
    {
        mappers = new HashSet<>();

        eventEngine = new EventEngine()
                .setLogger(LOGGER)
                .setEventType(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE))
                .setPersistEventOffset(true)
                .setEventQueueSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceProcessorQueueSize())
                .setEventHandler(this::process)
                .start(vertx, promise);
    }

    /**
     * Processes the incoming OTLP metric data contained in the provided {@link JsonObject} message.
     * <p>
     * This method performs the following steps:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Parses binary metric data from the message.</li>
     *     <li>Extracts metadata such as event source and object ID.</li>
     *     <li>Iterates through each {@code ResourceMetrics} object in the data.</li>
     *     <li>Extracts resource attributes to determine the service name.</li>
     *     <li>Sends test metric events if running in a test environment.</li>
     *     <li>Iterates over the metrics and processes each individually via {@code processMetric}.</li>
     *     <li>Dumps the processed metrics and logs processing time.</li>
     * </ul>
     * All resources are cleared after processing each resource metric to ensure no state leakage.
     * Errors during processing are logged but do not interrupt the loop.
     *
     * @param message a {@link JsonObject} containing the OTLP-encoded metric data under the key {@code EVENT},
     *                along with metadata such as {@code EVENT_SOURCE} and {@code OBJECT_ID}.
     */
    private void process(JsonObject message)
    {
        try
        {
            var metricsData = MetricsData.parseFrom(message.getBinary(EVENT));

            var eventSource = message.getString(EVENT_SOURCE);

            var objectId = message.getInteger(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_ID);

            addEventSource(eventSource);

            var startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();

            for (var resourceMetric : metricsData.getResourceMetricsList())
            {
                try
                {
                    var resource = resourceMetric.getResource();

                    var resourceAttributes = TraceConstants.parseAttribute(resource.getAttributesList(), null);

                    var serviceName = resourceAttributes.getString(TraceConstants.SERVICE_NAME, TraceConstants.UNKNOWN_SERVICE);

                    if (MotadataConfigUtil.getEnvironmentType().equalsIgnoreCase(ENV_TEST))
                    {
                        vertx.eventBus().send("trace.metric.test", new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.SERVICE_NAME, serviceName)
                                .put(TIME_STAMP, DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds())
                                .put(ID, objectId));
                    }

                    for (var scopeMetric : resourceMetric.getScopeMetricsList())
                    {
                        for (var metric : scopeMetric.getMetricsList())
                        {
                            processMetric(metric);
                        }
                    }

                    write(objectId, serviceName);
                }
                catch (Exception exception)
                {
                    LOGGER.error(exception);
                }
                finally
                {
                    clear();
                }
            }

            LOGGER.debug(String.format("Metric processing completed in %d ms", System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime));
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Processes a single {@link Metric} object based on its type and configuration template.
     * <p>
     * The method performs the following:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Retrieves the metric name and checks if it is defined in the {@code template} configuration.</li>
     *     <li>Identifies the type of metric data (e.g., GAUGE, SUM, HISTOGRAM, etc.).</li>
     *     <li>Delegates processing to the appropriate handler method based on the metric's data case.</li>
     *     <li>Processes the result further using {@code processResult} if the metric type was successfully handled.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * If the metric is not recognized in the template or the data case is {@code DATA_NOT_SET}, it is skipped.
     * Any exceptions during processing are caught and logged.
     *
     * @param metric the {@link Metric} instance to be processed, representing a single OTLP metric.
     */
    private void processMetric(Metric metric)
    {
        try
        {
            var name = metric.getName();

            var template = TraceCacheStore.getStore().getTemplate();

            if (template.containsKey(name))
            {
                var config = template.getJsonObject(name);

                // Handle different metric types
                var result = switch (metric.getDataCase())
                {
                    case GAUGE -> processGauge(metric, config);
                    case SUM -> processSum(metric, config);
                    case HISTOGRAM -> processHistogram(metric, config);
                    case SUMMARY,EXPONENTIAL_HISTOGRAM, DATA_NOT_SET -> null;
                };

                processResult(result, config, name);
            }

        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Processes the extracted metric result based on its type and template configuration.
     * <p>
     * The method handles different metric categories and updates internal data structures accordingly:
     * <ul>
     *     <li><b>Memory Metrics:</b> Aggregates per-instance memory usage based on "pool.name" and "type" attributes.</li>
     *     <li><b>Class Loading Metrics:</b> Extracts class count metrics and stores both total and per-instance values.</li>
     *     <li><b>Garbage Collection Metrics:</b> Aggregates GC action counts and durations per GC instance (name + action).</li>
     *     <li><b>Thread Metrics:</b> Differentiates between daemon and non-daemon threads and updates thread state counters.</li>
     *     <li><b>Other Metrics:</b> Treats all remaining metrics as scalar values and stores them directly in {@code scalarMetrics}.</li>
     * </ul>
     * If the result is {@code null} or empty, it is ignored.
     * Any exceptions during processing are caught and logged.
     *
     * @param result   the {@link JsonObject} containing parsed metric values keyed by attribute or metric names.
     * @param template the metric template {@link JsonObject} defining processing rules such as type and column mappings.
     * @param name     the name of the original metric, used for category determination (e.g., memory, GC, threads).
     */
    private void processResult(JsonObject result, JsonObject template, String name)
    {
        try
        {
            if (result != null && !result.isEmpty())
            {
                if (template.getString("type").equalsIgnoreCase("memory"))
                {
                    var column = template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN);

                    for (var index = 0; index < result.getJsonArray(column).size(); index++)
                    {
                        var key = result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey("pool.name", TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY)).getString(index) + SEPARATOR + result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey("type", TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY)).getString(index);

                        jvmMemoryMetrics.computeIfAbsent(key, val -> new HashMap<>()).put(column, result.getJsonArray(column).getNumber(index));
                    }
                }
                else if (isClassMetric(name))
                {
                    var count = result.getJsonArray(name).getInteger(0);

                    jvmScalarMetrics.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_PREFIX + name, count);

                    if (!name.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_CLASS_TOTAL))
                    {
                        jvmClassMetrics.put(template.getString("instance.value"), count);
                    }
                }
                else if (isGCMetric(name))
                {
                    var column = template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN);

                    for (var index = 0; index < result.getJsonArray(column).size(); index++)
                    {
                        var key = result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey("action.name", TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY)).getString(index) + SEPARATOR + result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey("name", TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY)).getString(index);

                        jvmGcMetrics.computeIfAbsent(key, val -> new HashMap<>());

                        var gcMetric = jvmGcMetrics.get(key);

                        gcMetric.put(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.ACTION_TOTAL, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), gcMetric.getOrDefault(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.ACTION_TOTAL, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), 0f) + result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.ACTION_TOTAL, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY)).getInteger(index));

                        gcMetric.put(buildMetricKey(GlobalConstants.DURATION, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), gcMetric.getOrDefault(buildMetricKey(GlobalConstants.DURATION, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), 0f) + result.getJsonArray(buildMetricKey(GlobalConstants.DURATION, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY)).getFloat(index));
                    }
                }
                else if (isThreadMetric(name))
                {
                    var column = template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN);

                    for (var index = 0; index < result.getJsonArray(column).size(); index++)
                    {
                        if (result.getJsonArray(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_DAEMON).getBoolean(index))
                        {
                            jvmScalarMetrics.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_DAEMON, jvmScalarMetrics.getInteger(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_DAEMON, 0) + result.getJsonArray(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_COUNT).getInteger(index));
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            var state = result.getJsonArray(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_STATE).getString(index);

                            updateThreadStateCounters(state, result.getJsonArray(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_COUNT).getInteger(index));
                        }
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    for (var counter : result.getMap().keySet())
                    {
                        jvmScalarMetrics.put(counter, result.getValue(counter));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Processes a {@link Metric} of type {@code GAUGE} and extracts its numeric value(s) based on the provided template.
     * <p>
     * This method performs the following:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Iterates over all data points in the gauge metric.</li>
     *     <li>Extracts the numeric value from each data point and converts it to a float.</li>
     *     <li>Maps the extracted value to the column name defined in the {@code template} using {@code ReportConstants.COLUMN}.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * Note: If multiple data points are present, the last value will overwrite previous ones for the same key in the result.
     * Any exception encountered during processing is caught and logged.
     *
     * @param metric   the {@link Metric} object of type {@code GAUGE} to be processed.
     * @param template the template {@link JsonObject} containing metadata such as the column name for mapping values.
     * @return a {@link JsonObject} containing the extracted gauge metric value mapped by its column name.
     */
    private JsonObject processGauge(Metric metric, JsonObject template)
    {
        var result = new JsonObject();

        try
        {
            for (var dataPoint : metric.getGauge().getDataPointsList())
            {
                result.put(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN), getNumberValue(dataPoint).floatValue());
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

        return result;
    }

    /**
     * Processes a {@link Metric} of type {@code SUM} and extracts its data points into a structured {@link JsonObject}.
     * <p>
     * This method performs the following steps:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Iterates over all sum data points in the metric.</li>
     *     <li>Extracts the numeric value from each data point and appends it to a JSON array under the key defined in the {@code template}'s {@code ReportConstants.COLUMN}.</li>
     *     <li>If the data point contains attributes, it maps additional instance-level values based on the {@code GlobalConstants.INSTANCE} configuration in the template.</li>
     *     <li>Each instance column is populated as a JSON array with corresponding attribute values.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * This allows associating each metric value with contextual attributes such as instance or label values.
     * If multiple data points exist, all corresponding values are collected into arrays for batch processing.
     * Any exceptions encountered during processing are caught and logged.
     *
     * @param metric   the {@link Metric} object of type {@code SUM} to be processed.
     * @param template the template {@link JsonObject} that defines mapping rules such as column names and instance keys.
     * @return a {@link JsonObject} representing the structured metric result, containing metric values and associated attributes.
     */
    private JsonObject processSum(Metric metric, JsonObject template)
    {
        var result = new JsonObject();

        try
        {
            for (var dataPoint : metric.getSum().getDataPointsList())
            {
                var attributes = TraceConstants.parseAttribute(dataPoint.getAttributesList(), null);

                result.getMap().computeIfAbsent(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN), val -> new JsonArray());

                result.getJsonArray(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN)).add(getNumberValue(dataPoint));

                if (!attributes.isEmpty())
                {
                    for (var key : template.getJsonArray(GlobalConstants.INSTANCE))
                    {
                        var instance = (JsonObject) key;

                        var column = instance.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN);

                        result.getMap().computeIfAbsent(column, val -> new JsonArray());

                        result.getJsonArray(column).add(attributes.getValue(instance.getString("key")));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

        return result;
    }

    /**
     * Processes a {@link Metric} of type {@code HISTOGRAM} and extracts data point values based on the provided template configuration.
     * <p>
     * This method performs the following operations:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Iterates over each data point in the histogram metric.</li>
     *     <li>Determines whether to extract the {@code sum} or {@code count} value based on the {@code aggregator} specified in the template.</li>
     *     <li>Stores extracted values under the key defined by {@code ReportConstants.COLUMN} in the template.</li>
     *     <li>Parses data point attributes and, if configured in {@code GlobalConstants.INSTANCE}, maps additional contextual fields (e.g., instance labels).</li>
     *     <li>Applies specific filtering logic for GC metrics to avoid duplicate total-action values.</li>
     *     <li>Supports custom aggregation logic per instance field using the same {@code aggregator} mechanism.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * If attributes are present, the method dynamically associates attribute values with their corresponding columns
     * as defined in the template. It ensures values are accumulated as arrays for batch processing.
     * <p>
     * All exceptions during parsing or value extraction are caught and logged.
     *
     * @param metric   the {@link Metric} object of type {@code HISTOGRAM} to be processed.
     * @param template the template {@link JsonObject} containing processing instructions including column mappings and aggregation logic.
     * @return a {@link JsonObject} with extracted metric values and their corresponding attribute/contextual mappings.
     */
    private JsonObject processHistogram(Metric metric, JsonObject template)
    {
        var result = new JsonObject();

        try
        {
            for (var dataPoint : metric.getHistogram().getDataPointsList())
            {
                var attributes = TraceConstants.parseAttribute(dataPoint.getAttributesList(), null);

                result.getMap().computeIfAbsent(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN), val -> new JsonArray());

                var aggregator = template.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR);

                if (aggregator != null && aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase("sum"))
                {
                    result.getJsonArray(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN)).add(dataPoint.getSum());
                }
                else if (aggregator != null && aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase("count"))
                {
                    result.getJsonArray(template.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN)).add(dataPoint.getCount());
                }

                if (!attributes.isEmpty())
                {
                    for (var key : template.getJsonArray(GlobalConstants.INSTANCE))
                    {
                        var instance = (JsonObject) key;

                        var column = instance.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN);

                        result.getMap().computeIfAbsent(column, val -> new JsonArray());

                        if (!(template.getString("type").equalsIgnoreCase("gc") && column.equalsIgnoreCase(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.ACTION_TOTAL, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY))))
                        {
                            result.getJsonArray(column).add(attributes.getValue(instance.getString("key")));
                        }

                        aggregator = instance.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR);

                        if (aggregator != null && aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase("sum"))
                        {
                            result.getJsonArray(instance.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN)).add(dataPoint.getSum());
                        }
                        else if (aggregator != null && aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase("count"))
                        {
                            result.getJsonArray(instance.getString(GlobalConstants.COLUMN)).add(dataPoint.getCount());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

        return result;
    }

    /**
     * Extracts the numeric value from a {@link NumberDataPoint}, returning it as a {@link Number}.
     * <p>
     * The method checks for the presence of an integer or double value in the data point:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>If {@code hasAsInt()} is true, returns the integer value via {@code getAsInt()}.</li>
     *     <li>If {@code hasAsDouble()} is true, returns the double value via {@code getAsDouble()}.</li>
     *     <li>If neither is present, returns {@code Double.NaN} to indicate an undefined or unsupported value.</li>
     * </ul>
     *
     * @param dataPoint the {@link NumberDataPoint} containing the numeric value to extract.
     * @return a {@link Number} representing the extracted value, or {@code Double.NaN} if not available.
     */
    private Number getNumberValue(NumberDataPoint dataPoint)
    {
        if (dataPoint.hasAsInt())
        {
            return dataPoint.getAsInt();
        }
        else if (dataPoint.hasAsDouble())
        {
            return dataPoint.getAsDouble();
        }

        return Double.NaN;
    }

    /**
     * Updates the configuration for all registered plugins based on the provided event source IP address.
     * <p>
     * This method performs the following:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>Iterates over each plugin in the {@code plugins} list.</li>
     *     <li>If the environment is {@code ENV_TEST}, uses a hardcoded IP ("172.16.8.135") to fetch the configuration item.</li>
     *     <li>Otherwise, uses the given {@code eventSource} IP to fetch the corresponding configuration item.</li>
     *     <li>Updates the plugin with the retrieved configuration item using {@link ObjectConfigStore}.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * This allows plugins to be dynamically updated with environment-specific configuration based on the source of incoming events.
     *
     * @param eventSource the IP address of the event source, used to retrieve the relevant configuration item.
     */
    private void addEventSource(String eventSource)
    {
        for (var plugin : TraceConstants.JVM_PLUGINS)
        {
            ObjectConfigStore.getStore().updateItemPlugin(plugin, MotadataConfigUtil.getEnvironmentType().equalsIgnoreCase(ENV_TEST) ? ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItemByIP("172.16.8.135") : ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItemByIP(eventSource));
        }
    }

    /**
     * Clears all internal metric data structures used during processing.
     * <p>
     * Specifically, this method resets:
     * <ul>
     *     <li>{@code memoryMetrics} – stores memory-related metric values.</li>
     *     <li>{@code scalarMetrics} – stores simple scalar metric values.</li>
     *     <li>{@code gcMetrics} – stores garbage collection metrics (e.g., count, duration).</li>
     *     <li>{@code classMetrics} – stores class loading-related metric values.</li>
     * </ul>
     * <p>
     * This ensures a clean state before processing the next set of metrics.
     */
    private void clear()
    {
        jvmMemoryMetrics.clear();

        jvmScalarMetrics.clear();

        jvmGcMetrics.clear();

        jvmClassMetrics.clear();
    }

    /**
     * Aggregates and serializes various JVM metrics (memory, GC, class, and thread)
     * and dispatches them to the datastore and monitoring pipeline.
     * <p>
     * This method processes the internally collected JVM metric maps, creates structured
     * JSON events for each category (memory, garbage collection, and class metrics), and
     * sends them to the event bus for persistence. Thread metrics are serialized into a binary
     * buffer format and also sent through the event bus.
     * <p>
     * Additionally, each event is enriched with the service name and forwarded to a
     * downstream system using the {@code send()} method.
     *
     * @param objectId the identifier representing the monitored JVM object instance
     * @param service  the name of the service associated with the metrics
     */
    private void write(Integer objectId, String service)
    {
        jvmMemoryMetrics.forEach((key, item) ->
        {
            try
            {
                var tokens = key.split(SEPARATOR_WITH_ESCAPE);

                var event = new JsonObject();

                item.forEach((counter, value) -> event.put(counter.replaceAll("_", DOT_SEPARATOR), value));

                event.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY, tokens[0])
                        .put(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_TYPE, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY), tokens[1])
                        .put(buildMetricKey(NMSConstants.INSTANCE_NAME, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY), tokens[0]);

                TraceConstants.write(event, tokens[0], objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_METRIC.getName(), builder, mappers);

                TraceConstants.send(new JsonObject().put(RESULT, new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_INSTANCE_KEY, new JsonArray().add(event))), objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_MEMORY_METRIC.getName(), TraceServiceConfigStore.getStore().getIdByService(service));

                LOGGER.info(String.format("Trace JVM Memory Metric : %s", event));
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                LOGGER.error(exception);
            }
        });

        jvmGcMetrics.forEach((key, item) ->
        {
            try
            {
                var tokens = key.split(SEPARATOR_WITH_ESCAPE);

                var event = new JsonObject();

                item.forEach(event::put);

                event.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY, tokens[1])
                        .put(buildMetricKey(NMSConstants.INSTANCE_NAME, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), tokens[1])
                        .put(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.ACTION_NAME, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY), tokens[0]);

                TraceConstants.write(event, tokens[1], objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_GC_METRIC.getName(), builder, mappers);

                TraceConstants.send(new JsonObject().put(RESULT, new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_GC_INSTANCE_KEY, new JsonArray().add(event))), objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_GC_METRIC.getName(), TraceServiceConfigStore.getStore().getIdByService(service));

                LOGGER.info(String.format("Trace JVM GC Metric : %s", event));
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                LOGGER.error(exception);
            }
        });

        jvmClassMetrics.forEach((item, value) ->
        {
            try
            {
                var event = new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_INSTANCE_KEY, item)
                        .put(buildMetricKey(NMSConstants.INSTANCE_NAME, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_INSTANCE_KEY), item)
                        .put(buildMetricKey(TraceConstants.JVM_CLASS_TOTAL, TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_INSTANCE_KEY), value);

                TraceConstants.write(event, item, objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_METRIC.getName(), builder, mappers);

                TraceConstants.send(new JsonObject().put(RESULT, new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_INSTANCE_KEY, new JsonArray().add(event))), objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_CLASS_METRIC.getName(), TraceServiceConfigStore.getStore().getIdByService(service));

                LOGGER.info(String.format("Trace JVM Class Metric : %s", event));
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                LOGGER.error(exception);
            }
        });

        var buffer = Buffer.buffer("UTF-8");

        TraceConstants.appendBytes(buffer, DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds(), DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_METRIC.getName(), objectId);

        buffer.appendIntLE(EMPTY_VALUE.length());

        buffer.appendString(EMPTY_VALUE);

        jvmScalarMetrics.forEach(item -> TraceConstants.updateBuffer(item.getKey(), CommonUtil.getString(item.getValue()), DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_METRIC.getName(), buffer, builder, mappers));

        vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DATASTORE_WRITE + DOT_SEPARATOR + DatastoreConstants.DatastoreCategory.TRACE.getName(), buffer.getBytes());

        TraceConstants.send(new JsonObject().put(RESULT, jvmScalarMetrics.put(TraceConstants.SERVICE_INSTANCE_KEY, service)), objectId, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_METRIC.getName(), TraceServiceConfigStore.getStore().getIdByService(service));

        LOGGER.info(String.format("Trace JVM Scalar Metric : %s", jvmScalarMetrics));
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given metric name corresponds to a JVM thread count metric.
     *
     * @param metricName the metric name to evaluate
     * @return {@code true} if it matches the thread count metric, {@code false} otherwise
     */
    private boolean isThreadMetric(String metricName)
    {
        return metricName.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_THREAD_COUNT);
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given metric name is related to JVM class loading.
     * <p>
     * Recognizes loaded, unloaded, and total class count metrics.
     *
     * @param metricName the metric name to evaluate
     * @return {@code true} if it is a class loading metric, {@code false} otherwise
     */
    private boolean isClassMetric(String metricName)
    {
        return metricName.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_CLASS_LOADED) || metricName.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_CLASS_UNLOADED) || metricName.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_CLASS_COUNT);
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given metric name corresponds to a JVM garbage collection (GC) duration metric.
     *
     * @param name the metric name to evaluate
     * @return {@code true} if it matches the GC duration metric, {@code false} otherwise
     */
    private boolean isGCMetric(String name)
    {
        return name.equalsIgnoreCase(TraceConstants.JVM_GC_DURATION);
    }

    /**
     * Updates thread state counters based on the given thread state and count.
     * <p>
     * Adds to the "live" thread count for states like waiting, blocked, and runnable.
     * Increments the "sleeping" thread count for the "timed_waiting" state.
     *
     * @param state the thread state (e.g., "waiting", "runnable", "timed_waiting")
     * @param value the number of threads in the given state to be added
     */
    private void updateThreadStateCounters(String state, int value)
    {
        if (state.equalsIgnoreCase("waiting") || state.equalsIgnoreCase("blocked") || state.equalsIgnoreCase("runnable"))
        {
            jvmScalarMetrics.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_LIVE, jvmScalarMetrics.getInteger(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_LIVE, 0) + value);
        }
        else if (state.equalsIgnoreCase("timed_waiting"))
        {
            jvmScalarMetrics.put(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_SLEEPING, jvmScalarMetrics.getInteger(TraceConstants.TRACE_JVM_THREAD_SLEEPING, 0) + value);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Constructs a namespaced metric key by combining the instance key and the metric key.
     *
     * @param metricKey   the base metric key (e.g., "type", "name")
     * @param instanceKey the instance key used as the prefix
     * @return a string representing the full metric key in the format: instanceKey::metricKey
     */
    private String buildMetricKey(String metricKey, String instanceKey)
    {
        return instanceKey + INSTANCE_SEPARATOR + metricKey;
    }

     * @throws Exception if any error occurs during shutdown
     */
    @Override
    public void stop(Promise<Void> promise) throws Exception
    {
        eventEngine.stop(vertx, promise);
    }

In `UIActionEventHandler.if()`: The UIActionEventHandler class handles events triggered by user interface actions and routes them to appropriate handlers.

This class is responsible for:

  • Processing UI-initiated events and actions
  • Routing events to appropriate handlers based on event type
  • Enriching events with additional context information
  • Managing notification delivery through various channels (email, integration channels)
  • Validating user inputs and configurations
  • Executing administrative actions (user management, configuration testing, etc.)
  • Handling file uploads and downloads

The handler acts as a bridge between the user interface and the backend systems, translating user actions into system events and routing them to the appropriate components for processing. It also handles the responses from these components and formats them for presentation to the user.

The class supports a wide range of UI actions including:

  • User authentication and authorization
  • Configuration testing (credentials, connections, etc.)
  • Report generation and export
  • Notification management
  • File uploads and downloads
  • System administration tasks

In `DNSUtil.sort()`: Sorts DNS server profiles by resolver type, prioritizing automatic (system-discovered) servers.

This method retrieves all DNS server profiles from the configuration store and sorts them based on their resolver type. Automatic DNS servers (those discovered from the system configuration) are given higher priority than manually configured servers.

Sorting Logic:

  • Servers with resolver type {@code AUTOMATIC} are placed first
  • Manually configured servers are placed after automatic ones
  • Within each category, the original order is preserved

This prioritization ensures that system-discovered DNS servers, which are typically more reliable and properly configured for the local network environment, are tried first before falling back to user-configured servers.

@return A {@link JsonArray} containing DNS server profiles sorted by priority, with automatic servers first, followed by manual servers

Engine for correlating availability events in the system.

The AvailabilityCorrelationEngine is responsible for:

  • Processing availability events (object up/down, instance up/down)
  • Correlating events to identify root causes of availability issues
  • Building and traversing dependency hierarchies to determine affected components
  • Managing the state of objects and instances during availability events
  • Suspending and enabling metrics based on availability status

This engine reduces alert noise by identifying the root cause of cascading failures and suppressing secondary alerts. It uses dependency information to determine which components are unavailable due to upstream failures versus those that have actual issues.

Central coordinator for visualization requests in the Motadata platform.

VisualizationManager is responsible for:

  • Receiving and processing visualization requests from clients
  • Routing requests to appropriate specialized managers based on visualization type
  • Tracking query progress and managing query timeouts
  • Aggregating and formatting responses from different data sources
  • Caching visualization results for improved performance
  • Publishing visualization results back to clients

This class maintains several maps to track query status, execution time, and cached results. It also implements timeout handling to abort long-running queries that exceed execution limits.

The manager supports various visualization types including metrics, events, availability, and compliance data, routing each request to the appropriate specialized manager.

In `RemoteEventRouter.send()`: Sends completed events to the appropriate handler based on event type.

This method routes completed events to their respective handlers on the event bus. Different event types are sent to different addresses:

- EVENT_DISCOVERY: Sent to EVENT_DISCOVERY_RESPONSE with 100% progress - EVENT_METRIC_POLL: Published to EVENT_METRIC_POLL_RESPONSE - EVENT_REDISCOVER: Sent to EVENT_REDISCOVER_RESPONSE - EVENT_TOPOLOGY: Sent to EVENT_TOPOLOGY_RESPONSE - EVENT_PLUGIN_ENGINE: Sent to EVENT_PLUGIN_ENGINE_RESPONSE - EVENT_CONFIG_UPGRADE_MANAGER: Sent to EVENT_CONFIG_RESPONSE_PROCESSOR

The method also handles reply contexts if the event requires a reply, and cleans up tracking maps after sending the event. @param event The completed event to be sent to its handler

In `MetricPoller.abort()`: Handles metrics that have been deleted or disabled.

This method: 1. Retrieves the deleted metric from the MetricCacheStore 2. Removes the associated event from the EventCacheStore 3. Logs information about the deleted metric 4. Sends an abort message to the appropriate event bus address

The abort message includes: - STATUS_ABORT status - ERROR_CODE_NO_ITEM_FOUND error code - A message explaining that the metric was deleted or disabled

In development mode, the message is published (broadcast to all consumers); in production mode, it's sent to a single consumer. @param id The ID of the metric to abort
